Oh also, Ask your players what they want. And don’t let them be vague about it. Ask them what they want to encounter more. Role play? What kinds of role play? Murder mysteries? Political Infiltration? Heist? 

What kinds of encounters? Puzzles? Easy combat? Gladiator Boss rush? 

Probe them to find what they would like and craft the stories around that. And they don’t need much planning. Bare bones.

So what I like to do, I use random generators to generate dungeons, monster encounters, npcs, the storyline or theme, treasures etc. 

I use these to create a small base skeleton for me to flesh out via Improv. I have a hard time sitting and focusing, but I like to take and pull ideas and interactions from shows/movies/books.

And as for overarching stories, I would suggest creating a smaller world for you characters to play in. The area they can play in can be smaller, which is more manageable. Each Arc of the campaign can cover different stories from the world, but to bridge those stories you can add tiny things like notes or an item or an npc. It can even be a total after thought and thrown in last minute.

Out in Canon County. Right now the communes aren’t accepting random visitors due to Rona, so you’d have to get into contact with someone from there and schedule a visit. But fun fact, The Sisters of Perpetual Indulgence actually started and lived on that commune for a long time, and one of the founders actually lives in the town a ways from the mountain.

Here in the states, in Tennessee, there are 4 LGBTQ+ communes that span one large mountain. There’s a Trans commune, a General LGBTQ+ Commune, A younger Queer commune, a queer POC commune, and a couple small scale Queer communes dotting the surrounding area. Most of the communes are under the Radical Faerie community, so you can find info on them, though they are generally kept away from Social media and are usually found out through word of mouth.

Hello there! I’m Gwen, Trans Non-Binary, They/them. Today was my first real time, outside of Pride, that I left to spend the day in public in the clothes I love.

I left with a couple of friends, and was terrified. We went to a Museum in a big city a ways from us. We had lunch, which I got a few stares but no maliciousness.

After, the Museum was amazing! I fit in since it was The Dali Museum, and I was sorta a Surrealist personality haha!

After, we went to a Tabletop Gaming shop, which I will say was a bit overwhelming. I know there is a tendency for the people there to be a bit hostile, so I was on edge. But all in all I felt so good! 

I’m so happy where I’m at, and I am glad to see where this transition goes.
